nodes.definition: Scripture is received as truthful revelation and bounds what the ontology may claim; interpretation remains corrigible.
nodes.example_needed: Genesis 1 read as ontology, not a journal article

nodes.definition: God is uncreated and self-existent; everything else is created, dependent and not divine.
nodes.example_needed: Psalm 100:3; Romans 1:25
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that the substrate is part of God

nodes.term: Creation is real from the beginning
nodes.definition: Genesis 1:1 is real instantiation; what follows is formation within created reality.
nodes.example_needed: earth, waters and darkness present before light

nodes.definition: Genesis 1 darkness is a real, unmanifested condition of creation, not nothing and not evil.
nodes.example_needed: a silent string under tension
nodes.common_misunderstanding: moral darkness read back into Genesis 1

nodes.definition: Observation, measurement, mathematical representation and prediction of how things behave.
nodes.example_needed: an equation predicting an orbit

nodes.definition: The account of what must be there for described behaviour to be possible.
nodes.example_needed: asking what a field is, not only how it behaves

nodes.definition: Predictive and mathematical success does not by itself settle what kind of reality is described.
nodes.example_needed: two interpretations of one quantum formalism

nodes.definition: Every ontology, scientific or theological, starts from assumptions that should be made visible.
nodes.example_needed: methodological naturalism as a choice

nodes.definition: Observation, mathematical description, inference, model, interpretation, theology, Scripture and RS hypothesis are different kinds of claim.
nodes.example_needed: a measured half-life versus its interpretation

nodes.definition: Claims fitting together: non-contradiction is necessary, but coherence also requires real connection, faithful translation across boundaries and preserved distinctions.
nodes.example_needed: a story whose parts do not contradict

nodes.definition: A model explains a bounded phenomenon internally.
nodes.example_needed: an equation fitting one regime

nodes.definition: Several adjacent domains integrate (chemistry with physics).
nodes.example_needed: molecular biology joining chemistry

nodes.definition: The whole account of reality — physics, life, persons, morality, history, Scripture — is connected, has valid interfaces, keeps its meaning through layers and cycles, stays stable under repair, keeps kinds of knowing accountable, and preserves its distinctions. It runs both ways (see bidirectional coherence).
nodes.example_needed: a worldview that explains physics but makes responsibility unintelligible fails globally

nodes.definition: Ordinary knowledge assembles the most coherent account from incomplete evidence under uncertainty.
nodes.example_needed: a doctor's diagnosis; a jury's verdict
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that the brain runs an RS algorithm

nodes.definition: A coherent account can still be false; agreement can harden an early error (false attractor).
nodes.example_needed: a confident consensus built on one mistaken premise

nodes.definition: Robust observation and logic rule out incompatible ontologies even when they cannot display the right one.
nodes.example_needed: a model contradicting measured light speed is ruled out

nodes.definition: Domains genuinely connected by intelligible transitions, not merely placed side by side.
nodes.example_needed: physics to chemistry to life

nodes.definition: A concept crossing a domain boundary keeps what is relevant without collapsing categories.
nodes.example_needed: physical consequence to moral responsibility

nodes.definition: A claim keeps its meaning through explanatory layers, and returns materially the same when translated round a cycle of domains.
nodes.example_needed: identity: physical → organism → person → body
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that plausible paragraphs add up to coherence

nodes.definition: From revision 2.7, proof is sufficient warrant under declared premises for an inferred relation to serve as a coherence factor; formal proof is conclusive relative to its axioms; RS is supported by a global coherence argument, not by experiment.
nodes.example_needed: a mathematical theorem versus an experimental result versus a coherence factor
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that proof means possessing the whole truth; that unproven means unconstrained

nodes.term: Structural analogy is not ontological identity
nodes.definition: Shared relational form across domains does not make the domains the same kind of thing.
nodes.example_needed: a letter and a nerve impulse both transmit; neither is the other
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that a shared grammar means a shared substance

nodes.definition: Material, biological, personal, spiritual and divine realities are genuinely distinct kinds.
nodes.example_needed: a body and a person

nodes.definition: RS must not contradict observation, measurement or successful mathematics; equally, the metaphysics that commonly travels with physics (container space, independent objects, fields as furniture) is a proposal tested for coherence, with no exemption from familiarity or consensus.
nodes.example_needed: measurement versus a picture of what was measured

nodes.definition: A real standing-between of things in which each conditions the other; interactional relation holds between complete things, constitutive relation partly makes things what they are — RS proposes the latter at the base.
nodes.example_needed: a knot exists only as the crossing of strands

nodes.definition: Independently located things share one interaction grammar: they affect one another, have compatible receptivity and commensurable quantities, and compose into stable structures. Every ontology must account for the common interface.
nodes.example_needed: granite from Hampshire and Western Australia
nodes.common_misunderstanding: a probability argument; a caricature of alternatives

nodes.definition: The assumption that reality is basically isolated objects in empty space with relations added afterwards.
nodes.example_needed: billiard balls in a void

nodes.definition: The proposed created relational order within which physical things are constituted and act; not matter, not a field, not God. Its spatiality (intrinsic, emergent or proto-spatial) is open.
nodes.example_needed: the order of a language within which words have their sense
nodes.common_misunderstanding: a hidden jelly or ether; a second world; a deity

nodes.definition: Creation as operating, distinguished from its origin; the domain of ordinary physical process.
nodes.example_needed: the difference between composing and performing

nodes.definition: Nothing affects anything across a gap of non-relation; every consequence depends on a relation connecting it to its source. Not a claim about travel or distance.
nodes.example_needed: a wave across a pond
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that this denies fields or long-range effects

nodes.definition: Minimal commitment: whatever is logically prior to, and conditions, actualisation. Working reading: constrained possibility, the admissible configurations and transitions and their weighting.
nodes.example_needed: the legal moves of chess, not a game
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that T0 is a realm, store or second world

nodes.definition: What kind of thing T0 is: an admissibility structure, a created potential order, a generative constraint architecture, the substrate itself prior to a particular actualisation, or something not yet formulated.
nodes.example_needed: three usages of the label across the project
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that possibility space is settled ontology

nodes.definition: What can happen next depends on present state and provenance; total admissibility is everything created order could bear. History changes the former without changing T0.
nodes.example_needed: a cracked stone can now split along its crack
nodes.common_misunderstanding: a one-way pipeline from hidden store to output

nodes.definition: Whether a transition is possible at all — a hard boundary of the possible.
nodes.example_needed: a door that exists versus one that does not

nodes.definition: How likely an admissible transition is relative to others; a weighting, not a permission.
nodes.example_needed: a well-worn path

nodes.definition: The coming-to-be of one admissible configuration among the possible.
nodes.example_needed: one game actually played

nodes.definition: Description by probabilities over defined possibilities; neutral between epistemic probability and ontic indeterminacy; not lawlessness.
nodes.example_needed: dice: each roll open, the distribution fixed

nodes.definition: RS hypothesis that actualisation is ontically stochastic: genuinely open among admissible options until it occurs, shaped by constraint.
nodes.example_needed: radioactive decay: open timing, exact half-life

nodes.definition: What a class of admissible changes leaves unchanged; one carrier or certificate of identity, not necessarily all of it.
nodes.example_needed: a conserved total; a knot's type

nodes.definition: Sameness of kind or state is preservation of the relevant relational equivalence class across admissible change, relative to what reachable future consequences can discriminate.
nodes.epistemic_category: ontological interpretation (author-supplied research) + RS model support
nodes.example_needed: two coins that look alike but one is counterfeit

nodes.definition: Functional, structural, equivalence-class and lineage-specific recovery are distinct; reconstruction is not automatically restoration of identity.
nodes.example_needed: a rebuilt organisation without its lineage
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that working again means the same again

nodes.definition: Being the same continuing individual, not merely an equivalent replacement; requires lineage and history beyond equivalence; open in RS research.
nodes.example_needed: two coins from the same die

nodes.definition: Past distinctions that survive in present relational structure; part of identity where consequential, safely ignored only where no reachable future can consume them.
nodes.example_needed: a bent paper clip; a forged signature's history
nodes.common_misunderstanding: provenance as a separate record or memory substance

nodes.definition: Whether any admissible future interaction could tell two states apart; the criterion for 'same' in the relevant domain.
nodes.example_needed: two keys alike until one is tried in the lock
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that it means what a human happens to measure

nodes.definition: A description that maps several distinct underlying states to one visible state; it can hide distinctions that later matter.
nodes.epistemic_category: mathematical + RS model result (constraint lab G1b)
nodes.example_needed: one coarse family label hiding many distinct exact laws
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that equal descriptions mean equal things

nodes.definition: Continued re-actualisation within the same relevant equivalence class.
nodes.example_needed: a flame maintaining itself

nodes.definition: Admissible change preserves an equivalence class, but destroyed distinctions are not recovered by conservation; recovery needs surviving information.
nodes.example_needed: an erased relation never repaired

nodes.definition: Past distinctions embodied in present relations so that they alter what is currently reachable, tendency, correlation or response; no separate memory substance required.
nodes.example_needed: metal fatigue depending on loading order

nodes.definition: A distinguishable state or relation that could make a difference to something other than itself.
nodes.example_needed: a dark mark on white paper

nodes.definition: A distinction in one relational condition is capable of constraining something other than itself; depletion of the source is one subcase, not the definition.
nodes.example_needed: a lighthouse; an atom emitting light; a spoken name
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that the source must lose what it transmits

nodes.definition: The dependency between source distinction and consequence preserves enough of the distinction for the consequence to depend on it; the carrier need not be a separate object, and at the most primitive level may be the relation itself.
nodes.example_needed: signal fires; a telephone call; a constitutive relation
nodes.common_misunderstanding: the carrier as a travelling thing

nodes.definition: The vehicle may change while the carried correlation is preserved.
nodes.example_needed: a wave moving through water whose molecules stay

nodes.definition: Another state becomes actual, or its admissible actualisation is constrained, because of the source distinction; arrival is not reception, and once-only is a property of transactional receivers.
nodes.example_needed: a letter read and acted on
nodes.common_misunderstanding: reception as mere arrival; reception as necessarily once-only

nodes.definition: Whether created order generates carrier and lineage architecture from minimal relations; not demonstrated — models used designed protocols.
nodes.example_needed: designed carrier protocols in every model so far
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that RS has shown carriers emerge by themselves

nodes.definition: What a receiver can register and how it responds (once, repeatedly, cumulatively, idempotently) is set by its own admissibility.
nodes.example_needed: the eye and radio waves; a thermostat; a ledger
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that every receiver must count arrivals once

nodes.definition: The grammar of consequential manifestation: distinction → preserved dependency → consequence. Presupposes no travel, metric space, intermediate object, encoding, layer stack, exactly-once reception or source consumption. Hypothesis: the operational form of consequential relation itself.
nodes.example_needed: seeing a stone in daylight
nodes.common_misunderstanding: packet transport; that soul or revelation is a physical signal

nodes.definition: Every receiver can transmit, so consequence forms a network: present actuality is received history and a source of what can happen next.
nodes.example_needed: molecule to cell to nerve to speech

nodes.definition: A distinction in one relational condition modifies the admissible actualisation or consequential state of another through a distinction-preserving dependency: by excluding, admitting or weighting states, constraining correlations, preserving an invariant or changing accessibility.
nodes.epistemic_category: RS working hypothesis (checked against constraint lab)
nodes.example_needed: a current gate weighting the next event; its initial value forgotten

nodes.definition: Transmissions compose in sequence and in parallel, and nest across scales.
nodes.example_needed: nerve impulse within perception within conversation

nodes.definition: Equal chances for each event do not fix how events are related; the joint process, covariance and global dynamics can differ.
nodes.example_needed: two crowds of coin-tossers, one independent, one in pairs

nodes.definition: Many independent or weakly dependent chance events average into a stable mean (laws of large numbers).
nodes.example_needed: steady tyre pressure

nodes.definition: A whole may be stable in mean, concentrated, exactly conserved or still stochastic in different respects; mean closure is not fluctuation closure, which is not full relational closure.
nodes.example_needed: same average, different fluctuations

nodes.definition: Consequence-aligned, state-dependent relations between stochastic events that stabilise aggregates; mean closure can hold while fluctuation closure stays open.
nodes.example_needed: two errors that cancel because they are tied

nodes.definition: What a local rule permits differs from what whole-system orchestration achieves; both must be stated.
nodes.example_needed: local cancellation exact but slower

nodes.definition: Stable, law-like aggregate behaviour arising from constrained stochastic processes.
nodes.example_needed: gas laws from molecular chaos

nodes.definition: Mathematics captures stable relations and invariants with great success without thereby being the reality.
nodes.example_needed: Navier–Stokes as an effective description of fluids

nodes.definition: Time is the ordering of change, directed by consequence (succession, revision 2.7), measured by comparing cadences; not an independent container.
nodes.example_needed: a pendulum compared with the turning Earth
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that clocks create time; that time is a container

nodes.definition: Matter is real, stable relational form, not primitive substance.
nodes.example_needed: a whirlpool or a knot

nodes.definition: Created order presenting itself to other things — detectable, encounterable; distinct from conscious awareness of it.
nodes.example_needed: the stone visible in daylight
nodes.common_misunderstanding: manifestation as an explanation of consciousness

nodes.definition: Divine purpose constrains what is possible; possibility constrains actualisation; the substrate itself intends nothing.
nodes.example_needed: a composer's intention fixing the instrument's range
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that the substrate is a mind

nodes.definition: Created runtime order is ordered without being intelligent, purposive or divine in itself.
nodes.example_needed: seedtime and harvest
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that lawful runtime means God is absent

nodes.definition: Boundaries make stable form possible rather than merely limiting.
nodes.example_needed: riverbanks making a river

nodes.definition: Because material order is relational at base, relational realities of life and persons are not bolted onto an alien, disconnected world.
nodes.example_needed: a world of sealed objects cannot ground promise-keeping

nodes.definition: Living things maintain, repair and reproduce organised form under hierarchical constraint; life is given and sustained by God.
nodes.example_needed: a cell repairing itself
nodes.common_misunderstanding: life as a vital fluid; life as nothing but chemistry

nodes.definition: A whole becomes real when its parts are coupled so that disturbance spreads and the whole retains properties no part has; from revision 2.6, tested by persistence beyond constituents, consequence as a unit, and multiple realisability (Chapter 8).
nodes.example_needed: an organism versus a crowd

nodes.definition: Real awareness, embodied and participating in shared reality, not reducible to physical configuration.
nodes.example_needed: seeing as an act, not only a signal

nodes.definition: A centre of awareness, relation, agency, address and responsibility; deeper than embodiment.
nodes.example_needed: Father and Spirit are persons without bodies

nodes.definition: Scripture's vocabulary for the inner person, given by God and not reducible to runtime configuration.
nodes.example_needed: Ecclesiastes 12:7
nodes.common_misunderstanding: soul as a physical signal or field

nodes.definition: The mode by which creaturely persons exist and act in created order; good and meaningful.
nodes.example_needed: Genesis 2:7

nodes.definition: Humanity's relational, representative, image-bearing calling before God.
nodes.example_needed: Genesis 1:27

nodes.definition: Physical possibility, operational capability and moral rightness are different questions.
nodes.example_needed: lying is possible, within ability, and wrong
nodes.common_misunderstanding: if it is possible it is permitted

nodes.definition: Fitting the order a thing or person is made for; in persons, a moral and relational reality, not only structural.
nodes.example_needed: an instrument in tune
nodes.common_misunderstanding: alignment as a physics measure of goodness

nodes.definition: Real, parasitic disorder of what is good: wrongdoing (wrong in itself) and its entrenchment as misalignment persists and spreads — not a rival substance.
nodes.example_needed: a lie: transmission that misdirects
nodes.common_misunderstanding: evil as a thing; or evil as unreal

nodes.definition: Finitude is good creaturehood; corruption is distortion.
nodes.example_needed: needing sleep

nodes.definition: God's work in Christ restoring and consummating creation and persons; not substrate repair.
nodes.example_needed: resurrection of the same person

nodes.definition: Embodied identity raised and transformed, continuous with the person who died.
nodes.example_needed: Luke 24:39

nodes.term: Divine action is not substrate process
nodes.definition: God acts as Creator and Lord, not as one more cause inside created admissibility.
nodes.example_needed: the resurrection of Christ

nodes.definition: Persistent, spatially individuated identity that can in principle be mechanically manipulated or relocated while preserving continuity as an identifiable entity. Narrower than physical; not widened to rescue a proposition.
nodes.example_needed: picking up the stone and carrying it
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that whatever physics finds is thereby material

nodes.definition: A real pattern or process of material carriers whose organisational identity is not an additional material entity; carrier, activity, identity and mathematical description kept apart. Some acquire entity-like individuality.
nodes.example_needed: a clap crossing a room
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that a sound wave is an extra object, or that its equation is the sound

nodes.definition: Handling relocates an identified entity preserving its identity; perturbation changes a condition without relocating a separate entity. Useful, not a universal classification.
nodes.example_needed: carrying the stone versus clapping
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that the difference is whether stuff travels

nodes.term: Emergence within matter vs emergence of matter
nodes.definition: Higher-order identities arise within matter (observed); material individuality arises within a non-material created order (RS hypothesis). The first does not demonstrate the second.
nodes.example_needed: a skyrmion in a magnet
nodes.common_misunderstanding: using emergence within matter as proof of B

nodes.definition: A: material fundamentality; B: non-material relational foundation with emergent matter; C: co-fundamental material and relational orders. Compared by explanatory burden with definitions fixed.
nodes.example_needed: the matched charges of proton and electron
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that design decides between them; that B is uniquely RS

nodes.definition: Comparative judgments of likelihood that are robust, conditional or unavailable, distinct from logical possibility and numerical probability, and valid without the latter.
nodes.example_needed: a hand one centimetre or one metre from an electric fence
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that no number means no comparison; that possibility carries a number

nodes.definition: Assigning unpriced properties to an explanatory entity whenever an interpretation needs them (the Harry Potter problem). Binds RS as strictly as its rivals.
nodes.example_needed: an invisible resident who explains every noise
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that it only afflicts rival views

nodes.definition: Knowledge of consequential behaviour does not fix intrinsic ontology, as a function's outputs do not fix its code; four classes of the unobserved kept apart.
nodes.example_needed: two drums that sound the same
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that unobserved means unreal, or that all will be observed

nodes.definition: A relational organisation that establishes, structures or constrains distinctions so they can take part in one coherent, consequential identity; transmit side.
nodes.example_needed: a radio modulator; a cello's body
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that it is a substance or a field

nodes.definition: A relational organisation able to preserve or reconstruct consequentially relevant identity from variations received through a compatible interface; receive side.
nodes.example_needed: the ear recovering a missing fundamental
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that cohering happens only in receivers

nodes.term: Receiver takes part in manifested identity
nodes.definition: A compatible receiver may help make an identity possible as consequentially manifested, without the source depending on reception.
nodes.example_needed: each observer's own rainbow
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that things exist only when perceived

nodes.definition: An identity stays coherent across changes of instantiation when the relations needed for its recognition or operation are preserved through compatible T-C-R.
nodes.example_needed: a phrase on cello, guitar and disc
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that a soul is a melody played on a body

nodes.definition: Distinction → relationship → organisation → higher-order identity, recursively; a higher-order identity is a distinction at the next order and a constraint on what sustains it.
nodes.example_needed: notes, chords, phrase, suite
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that stages are layers of reality; that every pattern is a new order

nodes.definition: A higher-order organisation produced by its components that then governs them (circular causality), as in the laser.
nodes.example_needed: a laser above threshold; a musical key

nodes.definition: Ultimate global coherence, perfectly comprehended and applicable, inseparable in the personal nature of God; no creature possesses it exhaustively.
nodes.example_needed: God's knowledge versus a doctor's diagnosis
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that it is an impersonal order of reality; that a human model is it

nodes.definition: The author's definition: the recursive refinement of partial understanding towards true logic through relational coherence within created runtime order.
nodes.example_needed: a diagnosis revised by a new test
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that revising a model revises reality

nodes.definition: A relation admitted for reuse with its scope, provenance, uncertainties and revision triggers visible.
nodes.example_needed: a law used within its tested regime

nodes.definition: Agreement among genuinely independent lines of inquiry strengthens warrant only as far as the independence is real; separate AI systems are not independent by default.
nodes.example_needed: the dodo known from accounts, bones, a head and a genome
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that many agreeing voices are many sources

nodes.definition: Intelligible error depends on genuine coherence; an error is a misassigned relation within a structure whose other parts may be sound.
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that every falsehood hides a truth; that error is moral evil

nodes.definition: Structural analogy, designed representation, causal connection within embodied personhood, and ontological identity (rejected).
nodes.example_needed: light and Christ; Romans 1:20; a spoken lie
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that representation is identity; that analogy is all there is

nodes.definition: An indefinitely deferred chain of dependent grounds cannot constitute ultimate grounding; the primitive created order is the foundation, fixed for creatures, not for the Creator.
nodes.example_needed: an explanation always postponed is never given
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that every mathematical infinity is inconsistent

nodes.definition: Constraints of the primitive order, and constraints following necessarily from an actual configuration even when it arose by chance.
nodes.example_needed: a cracked stone splits along the crack
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that implicit means weak; that necessity means determination

nodes.definition: A distinguishable occasion at which admissible actualisations are available; it can pass with nothing happening.
nodes.example_needed: the seed that could have germinated this spring
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that it is the same as possibility or admissibility

nodes.definition: The directed relational order of actual consequence, fundamental and prior to its measurement.
nodes.example_needed: the bell sounds because it was struck
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that a model's one-way rule creates it; that clocks create it

nodes.definition: The ordered pattern of opportunities (opportunity cadence) or of what occurs (actualisation cadence), not necessarily periodic; rhythm is recurrence with a cadence.
nodes.example_needed: a ferry calling twelve times, boarded four times

nodes.definition: Time's significance for persons, relative to capacity, conditions and history.
nodes.example_needed: an athlete's two minutes resting on months of preparation
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that it is a clock unit; that it measures worth

nodes.definition: An embodied human act and its moral reality are causally connected, not identical; created order is the theatre and language of moral consequence.
nodes.example_needed: a lie spoken with a tongue is also a wrong
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that the moral is physical; that the body is a mere sign

nodes.definition: Consequential history is carried in present relations with no separate ledger; consequence can persist where provenance is lost; God knows the whole.
nodes.example_needed: a deception's effects untraceable to the lie

nodes.definition: God subjected creation after the Fall; the author reads it as a deliberate realignment of primitive conditions so creation remains a truthful instructor; the mechanism is open.
nodes.example_needed: Genesis 3:17-19; Romans 8:20
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that Genesis describes microphysics; that every suffering is personal sin

nodes.definition: Wonder responds to coherence intelligible yet exceeding comprehension; beauty is the apprehensible expression of the patterns of goodness.
nodes.example_needed: John 14:6 read as way, truth and life
nodes.common_misunderstanding: that beauty is symmetry or preference
